risks: Minimal: repositioning is standard care. Risks are sleep disturbance, time taken from other night care, and blame of individual nurses for injuries.
consent: The round is care, not research; patients are told about it and may ask not to be woken for a round, which is recorded and respected. Staff take part as normal work.
data: Inspection and completion data are held by tissue viability with bed numbers and dates only; reports are at ward level; no nurse is identified.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients with darker skin tones, patients with cognitive impairment or delirium who cannot report pain, and patients with limited English are at risk of later detection. Touch-based assessment is part of cycle 3, injuries are reported by skin tone category, and interpreters are used when patients are asked about being woken.
effectiveness: Success is a sustained lengthening of the interval between injuries with stable late-dose and waking measures.
efficiency: Uses existing staff and inspection; the float nurse comes from the night bank when available.
costs: Recording sheets and staff time; no new budget.
partnerships: Night nurses from both wards, the night bank manager, tissue viability, and two patient partners from the hospital's patient panel.
rebPath: Registered by the hospital quality committee as quality improvement (QI-2026-054, 2026-09-02); no REB review required. Publication would follow SQUIRE 2.0 and the journal's policy for QI reports.
limitations: Two wards; uncontrolled; float availability outside the team's control.
summary: Minimal-risk QI with ward-level reporting, a right to decline night waking, and equity reporting by skin tone.
